query: How can melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties be determined accurately and efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family? State the physical rationale, expected quantitative performance, range of applicability, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive validation result that would rule out the proposed approach.

generation.hypothesis: A hybrid CALPHAD–machine‐learning framework that augments established binary and ternary liquid solution databases with data‐driven, multicomponent interaction corrections can predict melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid‐phase thermodynamic properties of high‐entropy alloys to within target accuracy across a broad composition space.
generation.material_initial_state: High‐entropy alloys composed of 4–8 metallic elements (each 10–35 at %) in a single disordered solid solution, no long‐range ordering.
generation.intervention: Apply CALPHAD calculations using assessed binary and ternary liquid solution models, then adjust multicomponent interaction parameters via a machine‐learning regression model trained on existing experimental fusion and liquid‐phase data.
generation.conditions: Ambient pressure, inert atmosphere; equiatomic and near‐equiatomic HEAs of 4–8 elements; temperature range bracketing predicted melting point.
generation.structural_mediator: Configurational entropy term and excess Gibbs energy corrections for the liquid phase, with ML‐derived additives capturing higher‐order interactions.
generation.mechanism: Machine‐learned corrections compensate for nonlinear multicomponent effects absent in lower‐order CALPHAD assessments, refining free‐energy surfaces to yield accurate phase‐equilibria and fusion properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: For ≥ 80 % of tested HEAs, melting temperature within ±50 K, enthalpy and entropy of fusion within ±10 %, and volume change at melting within ±5 % of experimental values.
generation.baseline: Standard CALPHAD using only binary/ternary data, which typically yields ±100 K error in Tₘ and ±20–30 % in fusion enthalpy.
generation.boundary: May not hold for alloys that form ordered intermetallic phases or exhibit strong short‐range order not represented in the training set.
generation.uncertainty: Prediction uncertainty rises outside the 4–8‐element, 10–35 at % per‐element domain; ML‐model variance suggests ±20–40 K for Tₘ and ±5–15 % for enthalpy.

falsification_experiment.design: Select 10 equiatomic HEAs not used in training, measure melting temperature (DSC), enthalpy of fusion (DSC integration), entropy of fusion (ΔH/Tₘ), volume change at melting (high‐temperature dilatometry), and liquid‐phase density; compare to predictions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If more than 50 % of the alloys exhibit deviations exceeding ±100 K in melting T, ±20 % in enthalpy of fusion, or ±10 % in volume change, the hypothesis is falsified.
